Sol said this so take it with a grain of salt:
> TMtx34f is a 3×4 matrix, so a concat method that calls MTXConcat is plausible. The current TMatrix34::concat uses scalar arithmetic, but that reconstructed code even accesses row 3 of a three-row matrix. I wouldn’t treat it as settled.

setRotX/Y/Z through MsMtxSetRotRPH seems less likely: the codebase has dedicated single-axis helpers, while RPH computes all three axes. A retail call to RPH would show the helper was used, but wouldn’t tell us whether a matrix method or the callback called it.

The stack gap could come from a 48-byte temporary matrix, frame alignment, or spills. I’d compare call targets, angle units, and multiplication order across several callbacks before changing the class. The concat idea is worth testing; the padding alone isn’t proof.
